problem:
Solve the inequality ${x}^{2}>12x$ and express the solution set in interval notation.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)\,⋃\,(${{field-3}}$,\,\infty )$
worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the terms to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & >12x \\ {x}^{2}-12x & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-12x$ lies **above** the $x$-axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-12x & =0 \\ x(x-12) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=0$ and $x=12,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/387b02ad3416b06b3f86f12c99b921800ab4b86f39be9da0fc48883952d366d2.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
{x}^{2}-12x>0,
$$

 
we look for the part of the parabola that is **above** the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x<0$ or $x>12.$

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-\infty ,0)⋃(12,\infty ).$
